The comment names the push cache scope missing the pull_request run's cached pass, gives the PR #185 timings (26 s, versus two push runs of 16 min each), labels them as from the request, and cites D125. The pull_request, workflow_dispatch and cron lines are untouched (ci.yml lines 21-25).

criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new decision entry, numbered after the latest, with alternatives and the PR #185 timings (pull_request run 26 s via cached pass; two push runs ~16 min; landing waited 17m51s), labeled as taken from the request.

The diff only adds lines.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry under [Unreleased] (Changed) describing the push trigger limit.
criteria.evidence: A new bullet sits under `### Changed`, right after the D124 bullet, inside `## [Unreleased]` (line 8; the next release heading is at line 1560). It describes the push-to-main limit and points to D125.

criteria.criterion: Header comment in ci.yml that refers to the cache scope remains consistent with the new trigger.

summary: Pass: the change does what the request asks. In ci.yml, the push trigger now runs only on main, with a comment that gives the reason (cache scope) and the PR #185 timings. The other triggers (pull_request, workflow_dispatch, the weekly schedule), the job names and the cache logic are unchanged. docs/decisions.md gets a new D125 entry, numbered after D124, with alternatives. Its timings are labeled as taken from the request, and it lists the post-landing check of one run per commit as a follow-up, not as done. CHANGELOG.md has a matching bullet under [Unreleased] → Changed. Only the three named files changed. The landing code's wait for 'fmt, clippy, tests' matches the job by name and does not filter by event, so the pull_request run still satisfies it. fmt, clippy and the 1239 tests passed in Athena's recorded checks on this tree; I did not rerun them. One accepted side effect, which the docs state: pushes to other branches, including athena/records, no longer start CI.
